transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (AE), Priya (SE), Marco (SE), Sales Enablement slice

Summary:
Quick internal enablement run for messaging + competitive positioning. Focused on demo flow, handling latency vs cost questions, and security FAQs. Practiced a short role-play with typical objections.

Topics:
- Core messaging: production economics, unified runtime, predictable latency
- Competitive differentiators: Dedicated, Private, Optimize, Console
- Demo practice: cold start, KV cache, batching, fallback policies
- Common security questions: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): alright folks, thanks for joining, this is a 45 to 60 min run, mostly practice of the customer-facing script, try to keep things real, i'll play the AE, priya you'll lead the deep demo bits, marco gives feedback
[00:18] Priya (SE): cool yep, starting with the one-liner: Redwood Inference helps teams run high-performance LLM inference across hosted, dedicated and private deployments with predictable latency and cost trade-offs
[00:35] Marco (SE): maybe call out "production economics" earlier — customers love the cost per token angle, but careful not to sound like only about price
[00:50] Jordan (AE): okay role-play 1, i'm going to be a concerned platform engineer, ask you about VPC and private deployment, go
[01:05] Priya (SE): sure, thanks — for regulated workloads you can use Redwood Private which gives a customer-managed control plane, VPC peering, and optional on-prem bundle; we support KMS integrations and HSMs for key management and full audit logs
[01:22] Jordan (AE): what about SOC2 and SSO?
[01:26] Priya (SE): we are SOC 2 compliant, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC in the console, and you can pull detailed token-level cost and latency breakdowns for audit or chargeback
[01:40] Jordan (AE): great, question on latency — we have a 50ms SLO for a feature, can you meet that?
[01:47] Priya (SE): depends on model and sequence length; for shorter seqs our hosted API with optimized kernels and continuous batching can meet low 10s of ms on the right model, but if you need predictable tail latency you can use Dedicated pools with pinned capacity and autoscale policies to keep latency under a target
[02:05] Marco (SE): add that we can route by policy — latency-first vs cost-first — and there are fallbacks to compatible quantized variants if capacity is constrained
[02:20] Priya (SE): yes and also mention caching — prefix/KV cache reduces cost and latency for repeated context, and Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and quantization profiles based on observed workload
[02:35] Jordan (AE): objection: customers say "we can just use OpenAI/Anthropic — why Redwood?"
[02:42] Priya (SE): answer: two things — first, developer experience and consistency across deployment modes, you can start on hosted and move to dedicated or private without rearchitecting; second, unit economics — our Optimize tooling + caching + smart routing typically reduces per-token cost in production when workloads are predictable
[02:58] Jordan (AE): another objection: "what about model quality/regressions?"
[03:05] Priya (SE): we have model catalog with vetted profiles, version pinning, and rollout features (canary/A-B and automatic fallback) plus quality-monitoring tied to eval prompt sets so you can detect regressions before they reach prod
[03:20] Marco (SE): practice the line that it's not just model access; it's the serving layer and operational tooling that saves engineering time and reduces outages
[03:32] Jordan (AE): switching to demo script — priya, walk us through the cold start flow and KV cache example, try to intentionally trip common questions
[03:45] Priya (SE): demo step 1: show console, route config: pick model, set batching policy and autoscale threshold; step 2: run a sample request to show cold-start time (note: imperfect transcription, numbers approximate)
[04:05] Priya (SE): [shares screen] starting request... cold start latency ~ 420ms on this model in our dev region (note: this is synthetic, depends on hardware); then warm request after KV cache and batching is ~ 45ms
[04:25] Jordan (AE): customer interruption: "that difference seems big, why?"
[04:29] Priya (SE): explain cold-start overhead — model weights load, kernel initialization; with Dedicated you keep GPUs warm, and our autoscale keeps a small buffer to reduce cold starts. also prefix/KV cache avoids recomputation for repeated context
[04:45] Marco (SE): mention quantized model variants — lower precision cuts memory and reduces cost with slight tradeoff in output quality; Redwood Optimize suggests which workloads are safe to quantize
[04:58] Jordan (AE): another common ask: "can we run on-prem with air-gap?"
[05:03] Priya (SE): yes we have an on-prem package; control plane can be private and you can still use our orchestration layer, plus we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. caveat: telemetry and support model differ for air-gapped installs, that's part of the enterprise license conversation
[05:20] Jordan (AE): good — now a competitive role-play: i play CTO leaning toward Vertex AI, you defend Redwood vs Vertex
[05:30] Priya (SE): Vertex has good cloud-native tooling but its inference pricing and ops story can be more fragmented; Redwood differentiates with a unified runtime tuned for LLMs, transparent performance benchmarks, and explicit levers for cost/latency trade-offs — plus the Dedicated model for predictable throughput
[05:50] Jordan (AE): objection: "we already have internal infra on GCP, why migrate?"
[05:55] Priya (SE): migration is incremental — you can start by pointing non-sensitive traffic at hosted, then move high-value workloads to Dedicated or private. we also provide model variants and tooling to replicate performance on customer infra via our private deployment options
[06:12] Marco (SE): tip — call out that our runtime includes attention optimizations and kernel selection based on sequence length distribution; that's a tangible engineering differentiator
[06:30] Priya (SE): demo segue to failure modes: show automatic fallback policy where if Dedicated capacity is constrained requests route to a lower-cost compatible variant in hosted tier and we surface that in logs and the console
[06:48] Jordan (AE): question: "what's the observable visibility for SREs?"
[06:52] Priya (SE): Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis — we can also export traces to customer's observability stack
[07:05] Marco (SE): practice the answer about compliance: "we'll provide audit logs, SAML SSO, and SOC2 reports, and support customers through security reviews"
[07:18] Jordan (AE): ok let's do lightning role-plays: i'll fire rapid objections and you respond concisely
[07:24] Jordan (AE): "how much does Dedicated cost?"
[07:26] Priya (SE): depends on commit size and instance types — give ranges and say we'll follow up with pricing sheet; emphasize reserved capacity reduces per-token variability
[07:35] Jordan (AE): "what about data residency for EU customers?"
[07:38] Priya (SE): we support region pinning and Private deployments; for EU-only needs we recommend Private or dedicated in EU regions with customer-managed keys
[07:46] Jordan (AE): "we have hard SLAs for latency"
[07:48] Priya (SE): Dedicated with pinned pools and SLAs is the right call; also can use multi-region fallback for availability
[07:56] Marco (SE): small note — when discussing SLAs, call out typical metrics we can promise and the escalation process (support tier)
[08:06] Jordan (AE): demo nit: transition between slides was slow, maybe tighten the script to avoid dead air
[08:12] Priya (SE): ack, will tighten; also add a one-slide appendix for HW sizing examples and typical latency ranges by model class
[08:24] Jordan (AE): competitive messaging refinement: when comparing to OpenAI, avoid negative framing; say "we offer more deployment flexibility and operational controls while maintaining easy API parity"
[08:36] Priya (SE): note on transcription — sometimes model and product names were transcribed wrong; call out to not rely on verbatim transcript in external comms
[08:50] Jordan (AE): practice closing: recap next steps and ask for commitment to dry run with 2 customer accounts next week
[08:58] Priya (SE): recap: update script, share competitor one-pager, record latency clip, schedule dry run — all noted
[09:10] Marco (SE): feedback loop — we'll collect common objections and fold them into the objection-handling doc in the sales repo, plus add three canned responses for the AE playbook
[09:26] Jordan (AE): end of practice, good session — final notes: avoid deep technical rabbit holes in discovery; steer to a later technical deep dive if the customer wants kernel-level details
